title: Listings at the Threshold
description:
A real estate office in Gangnam. Evening clung to the glass door. {name} sat alone at the consultation desk.

Three listings priced around 2.5 billion won lay on the desk. The bold figures were asking prices, and no line bore a buyer's name. {name}'s assets had reached the office's 2.5-billion-won threshold. The notebook's first page held a 3-billion-won goal. The assets screen already showed whether the current figure sat below, at, or beyond that goal, but none of the homes on the desk was his yet.

Behind the single figure on the account and assets screens lay five years of money in and out, choices that had moved his assets, and time that had passed. The figure showed how far he had come, not what he had left behind.

Beside each asking price were blanks for acquisition tax, the brokerage fee, and cash to keep after moving. A fresh line opened between a price that looked affordable and one he could survive after paying. No signed purchase agreement or registration receipt lay on the desk, and no key had been handed over.

Reaching the 2.5-billion-won threshold had brought {name} through the office door. At the threshold, he could open Father's entry in his contacts or push through the glass door and walk one block of Gangnam-daero.

{name} stopped with the listings still unfolded. The choice now was not a home, but the first action to take at this threshold.

choices.text: Open Father's name in his contacts
choices.result_text:
{name} found Father in his contacts and opened the entry. Beneath the saved name were only a call button and old records.

He held a finger above the button but did not press it. A contact name looked the same whether the person was alive or gone. His lips formed the words he did not send: he had not bought a home, his assets had reached the 2.5-billion-won threshold, and he was comparing the current figure with the first goal of 3 billion won.

No outgoing time, ring, or answer appeared on the screen. {name} left Father's entry open and walked out of the office carrying only the listings.

choices.text: Walk Gangnam-daero alone, slowly
choices.result_text:
{name} pushed through the glass door and stepped onto Gangnam-daero in the same evening. He carried no contract, only the unfolded listings.

Two lights changed over the length of one block. His lower back and calves tightened after the long sitting, and {name} slowed at the second crossing.

Five years ago, entering this street had felt like looking into someone else's life. Now he could ask prices and do the sums, but neither gave him ownership. When the second light changed, he swallowed the urge to say "I've arrived" as if the listings were a deed, then crossed.

title: The Fifth Winter
description:
The fifth winter came.

{name} opened the assets screen. Closed it. Didn't open it again.

Not 3 billion. That much was clear now.
Not a number you flip in the weeks remaining.

The goal he'd set five years ago — Gangnam. Those words felt far away now.
Was it failure? The question rose, and strangely didn't linger long.

Snow began to fall beyond the window of the room where he now lived.
The room and the view had changed more than once, but tonight this place was unmistakably {name}'s own.

It was the same winter as five years ago. The person watching it was not the same.
description_low_mental:
The fifth winter.

{name} didn't even have the strength to open the assets screen.

Not 3 billion. Gangnam was far.
The fact pressed on his chest — and what scared him more was how used to the weight he'd become.

When did it get like this.
A life where just getting up burned all of the day's energy.

Outside, snow fell.
{name} watched it for a long time. Thinking nothing.

choices.text: Write down what these five years left you
choices.result_text:
He opened the notebook.

Gangnam: didn't make it.
Under that, slowly, he wrote other things.

Five years survived. Debt paid off. People he'd come to know. Things he'd learned.
No longer fooled. The number of times he fell and got back up.

In numbers it wasn't 3 billion.
But what was written in the notebook — those were things 3 billion couldn't buy.

{name} closed the notebook. The snow kept falling.

choices.text: Just watch the snow — sort nothing out
choices.result_text:
He decided not to sort it out.

Whether it was five years well-lived or poorly-lived — there was no need to conclude it now.
That only comes into view later, from further away.

For now, snow was simply falling.
{name} sat by the window and watched.

Neither warm nor cold, a strangely peaceful night.

title: A Call That Might Be the Last
description:
Late at night, a call from Father.

Not a special day. Just a Wednesday night.

"You up?"
"Yeah. Still awake."

Five years ago this call would have been awkward. With six years of debt between them, both avoiding the subject.

But now it was different.

"Minjun."
"Yeah."

Father paused. A man silent his whole life seemed about to say something.

choices.text: "Dad, I never said it — but it was okay. All of it."
choices.result_text:
The other end went quiet.

For a long time.

Then Father said something he'd never said in his life.
"...Thank you. And I'm sorry. Both."

{name} looked at the ceiling. His eyes burned.
The six years of debt, the five years of struggle — all of it grew small before this one call.

"Dad. Gangnam or not, I'm coming down soon. Let's eat together."
"...Yeah. Let's do that."

choices.text: "Is something wrong? Your voice sounds..."
choices.result_text:
"No. I just... wanted to hear your voice."

It was the first time Father had said that.

{name} held the phone to his ear for a long while.
There was so much to say, but none of it came out.

In the end, all he said was "...Me too, Dad."

There are nights when that's enough.
After hanging up, {name} watched out the window a long time. Gangnam far or near, tonight that didn't matter.

title: Page Seven
description:
Sangchul arrived before the appointed time. A seven-page offer and two paper cups sat on the meeting-room table. He pushed the less-cold cup toward {name} and tapped the figure on page one.

"You made it all the way to the end. Lock this today and 3 billion won becomes a number we can discuss."

Page seven held a blank marked CONSENTING PARTY'S NAME. The addendum beneath it borrowed Daeun's name in exchange for priority over her weekends and nights. When {name} pulled the staple, the tablet in his bag briefly lit up with his father's old guarantee PDF. The two documents hid the scope of liability in sentences of the same shape.

"Does Daeun know?"
Sangchul swallowed cold coffee. "She'll sign for herself. You explain it."

He pushed over the calculator. The figure was close to the goal. Daeun's blank name field was directly under his fingertip.

texts: The calendar still held the slash after seven on Thursday and the two hours that could no longer be sold. Sangchul's today demanded that {name} turn that line back into contract time.
The first Sunday of next month remained circled on both screens, with neither person having marked the promise complete. Sangchul's seven pages demanded an answer before that unfinished day did.
Beside the line joining the clinic record to family calls were Daeun's words: TELL ME BEFORE. When Sangchul pushed over the calculator, {name} saw the promise to speak before stopping.

choices.text: Set Father's guarantee PDF beside it. Ask whether Sangchul can review his own offer.
choices.result_text:
{name} opened his father's guarantee PDF beside the offer. The two name fields shared one screen.

"Can the person who brought the deal review it too?"

Sangchul did not pick up the red pen. "If I read my own contract for you, that isn't verification. You hear my word twice. Bring both documents to the old office. I can at least tell you where my interests collide."

{name} said he would give no answer today. Sangchul left the calculator where it was. Its blinking display and the cold coffee remained on the table.

choices.text: Cover Daeun's name field. Ask what terms remain without her name.
choices.result_text:
{name} covered Daeun's name field with a memo slip.
"How far does this go without her name?"

Sangchul asked, "Do you really have to take it out now?" but finally turned the calculator around. With every deleted line, the figure stepped lower. The goal moved farther away, but so did the name the contract had meant to borrow in secret.

While the printer released the new figure, Sangchul never touched the cold coffee.

choices.text: Take the addendum to Daeun first.
choices.result_text:
{name} packed the papers with the signature field blank. Behind him, Sangchul called out.
"The deadline is today."

"So is Daeun's time to read it."

Beside the café's closing checklist, Daeun opened the page bearing her name before the page of figures. Her finger stopped on WEEKENDS AND NIGHTS.
"Tell me what I'm lending you first, Minjun. Is it my name or all the time after it? I decide after that."

title: The Owner of the Cold Coffee
description:
The old office door did not open on the first push. When {name} leaned a shoulder into it, Sangchul kicked a pile of mail clear from the other side. Two paper cups stood on the desk. A skin had formed over one coffee.

"You made it all the way to the end."

{name} set Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF beside the final offer. Sangchul looked at the name fields before the amounts.

"The papers didn't lie back when your father signed either. Nobody read what their words meant between people."
"Read these with me."

Sangchul swallowed a mouthful of cold coffee.
"If I make the offer and review it too, that's not verification. That's my word repeated. If you still want my time, you decide where to spend it."

He placed a red pen between the documents.

texts: Jaehyuk's chat held the sent refusal with its time while the input remained open. The PDF signature line was still blank, so {name} placed before Sangchul the screen where refusal—not silence—had been recorded.

Black letters and an authentication time filled the guarantee field, while Jaehyuk's chat contained no sentence from {name}. Sangchul looked at the completed signature first and asked what had been read before that name entered it.
A block notice sat at the bottom of Jaehyuk's chat; the input and call button were gone. The signature line remained blank, but the hand that had closed contact was now asking Sangchul for review.

choices.text: Ask him to circle only the single most dangerous clause.
choices.result_text:
Sangchul drew one line from the scope of liability in the guarantee PDF to the name field in the offer. The red circle was small, but it held both pages in its bite.

"If you can't explain this, you can't sign. Not to me. Not to that person."

{name} took back the pen. Sangchul said nothing more and slid his own coffee farther from {name}.

choices.text: Ask whether the terms would change with Sangchul's name in the field.
choices.result_text:
Sangchul did not smile. He laid his business card over the blank, then took it away.
"Would my name make it safe? Or just make it easier because you'd owe someone else?"

{name} had no answer. Sangchul folded the card in half and dropped it into the wastebasket. Between the two cold coffees, the name field remained empty.

choices.text: Fold the papers and ask exactly how much of his time the review took.
choices.result_text:
"Forty minutes." Sangchul answered without checking a clock.

{name} wrote the time on the cover. He did not offer money or promise a next meeting.

At the door, Sangchul held out a fresh paper cup. Its lid was closed and the coffee was still hot. {name} accepted it, but opened the door with his own hand.

title: Four at the Table
description:
Four people sat inside the glass meeting room. Sangchul had the offer he had brought and a red pen. Jaehyuk had his own guarantee PDF. Daeun had a copy opened to the field for her name. Only {name} had a calculator in front of him.

Sangchul opened the returns table. "Lock it today and these are the terms. But don't call it safe just because I reviewed the deal I brought." He left the red pen down. Jaehyuk's knee bounced as he cut in. "Minjun, I know what you left in the guarantee field. But here, at this table, let's read all the way through what my document binds."

Daeun peeled the sleeve from a paper cup gone cold and laid it across the name field. "You two finished the whole conversation with my name before I even answered."

Sangchul looked at Jaehyuk. Jaehyuk looked at {name}. Daeun let neither man choose where she looked. The wall clock cut the time left before the transfer deadline into small pieces.

texts: On the table, Jaehyuk's chat showed the guarantee refusal beside an open input. There was no read mark, but the sent sentence and blank signature line now lay together before Jaehyuk's chair.
Black letters and an authentication time already occupied {name}'s field in Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF. Beside that field, Jaehyuk now had to read his own liability aloud.
Jaehyuk's chat input was gray and locked, and its call button had vanished. Yet he occupied the chair across the table, forcing the document's liability back into the room outside the blocked screen.
Sangchul's red circle bit both the liability clause and the name field, but he had already said he could not call it safe. Here too, the circle marked his conflict rather than an answer.
Sangchul had folded his own business card and thrown it away; the name field remained blank. He sat at the table unable to substitute his name for safety.

FORTY MINUTES was written on the offer cover, and the fresh cup Sangchul had handed over stood before {name}. Between the hot cup from the old office and today's cold coffee, the borrowed review time became harder to ignore.

The phone photograph preserved the unbroken red circle across both originals with its capture time. {name} left that frame open too, so the proposer's review could not masquerade as independent verification.

choices.text: Open the main contract, addendum, and name field all at once.
choices.result_text:
{name} pulled the staple and laid the offer, addendum, and Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF in one row. Sangchul read the offer amount aloud. Jaehyuk read the term of his liability. Daeun pulled the last page closer and read CONSENTING PARTY'S NAME, then PRIORITY OVER WEEKENDS AND NIGHTS.

"Why are these two sentences on different pages?" Daeun asked. Sangchul finally picked up the red pen and connected them. Jaehyuk's knee stopped bouncing. {name} turned off the calculator.

choices.text: Give Sangchul the first question.
choices.result_text:
Sangchul laid Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF over the offer.
"If Daeun's name comes out, does the deal fail, does your liability grow, or does my share shrink? Pick one."

Jaehyuk's hand stopped above the calculator. "You brought the deal too."

"Which is why my answer can't be verification. I'm asking for yours." Sangchul set the red pen down. Daeun did not watch the two of them. She watched {name}, asking with her eyes who had postponed answering her.

choices.text: Hand the contract to Daeun first.
choices.result_text:
Daeun read from the last page backward: the field for her name, the term of liability, the date she could withdraw.

"Minjun, which parts do I actually get to choose? Does not using my name count?"

Before {name} could answer, Jaehyuk put down the pen. Sangchul took out a blank sheet and placed it before Daeun. "Of course it does. Write every term in your own hand." The first record of the meeting was Daeun's question, not the projected return.

title: Who Owns the Line
description:
9:47 p.m. The corners of the papers before the four of them had worn in different directions.

Sangchul spoke first. "The limit drops without Daeun's name. Those are the terms I brought. But a red line from me doesn't make them safe." Jaehyuk pressed his guarantee PDF flat with one palm. "Minjun, my name is on the line too. You aren't the only one using somebody else's."

Daeun ignored the figure and looked at {name}. "I'm not asking how much you make. I'm asking how far you meant to use my name and my time before you asked me."

{name} opened the transfer-lock screen. Thirteen minutes remained. Sangchul put down the red pen. For the first time, Jaehyuk took his hand off the calculator. There was one blank on the page and three people waiting for an answer.

texts: The offer, addendum, and guarantee PDF still lay in one row after Sangchul, Jaehyuk, and Daeun had read the amount, liability term, and name field aloud. With {name}'s calculator dark, no figure could answer for any of them now.

Sangchul had asked the first question and set down the red pen, while Daeun had kept her gaze on {name}. The proposer had asked but could not verify the answer, and that conflict remained on the table.
After Sangchul placed the blank sheet before Daeun, her question—WHAT DO I GET TO CHOOSE—became the meeting's first record, ahead of the projected return. It now demanded {name}'s answer.

choices.text: Remove that name and recalculate the smaller terms.
choices.result_text:
{name} drew a diagonal line across Daeun's name field. Sangchul read out the smaller limit. Jaehyuk read again the sentence that expanded his guarantee.

Daeun left her copy open on the table. "At least this line never required me to draw it."

Sangchul wrote down the new figure but did not add the word safe. The original blank still showed faintly through the diagonal line.

choices.text: Postpone the decision. Let the consenting person write the limits and deadline.
choices.result_text:
The transfer alert sounded once. {name} turned the screen facedown.

Daeun wrote the permitted scope and an end date in her own hand. At the bottom she added, I DO NOT CONSENT BEYOND THESE TERMS. Sangchul listed the clauses he had not verified below it. Jaehyuk stood holding his guarantee PDF, unable to fold it. No one took an original. Each of the four left with only a copy.

choices.text: Declare the review finished and resume signing on the original terms.
choices.result_text:
When {name} released the transfer lock, the figures began moving again. Sangchul pushed the offer toward him but said, "Reading it isn't consent from me."

Jaehyuk swallowed a breath of relief and slid his guarantee PDF beneath the contract. Daeun did not take the pen. She tucked away her copy. "My name is still inside my answer."

No one stormed out. That made the second hand and the distance between the four of them sound even louder.

title: Filing Number 227
description:
A cord tethered the blue pen to the filing counter. The clerk looked from the contract to the identity copy, then covered Daeun's name field with one finger.

{name} opened every original message and signed sheet that remained from the day he first showed Daeun Sangchul's offer. Any request for explanation or refusal she had actually sent was still on the screen. If she had written a scope and deadline, her hand remained on the original. An unanswered question had produced no message; an unwritten limit had produced no signature.

The clerk separated phone from paper. "A conversation cannot replace the scope of consent. Without a handwritten scope and deadline, obtain new confirmation or recalculate in your own name."

An old identity copy in a separate envelope was not current consent. A smaller estimate in {name}'s name alone was also in the bag. The number display chimed. "Which document are you filing?"

choices.text: Honor the refusal that exists—or the consent that never arrived—and withdraw.
choices.result_text:
The clerk checked the refusal if one actually remained, or the absence of consent if none did. WITHDRAWN landed in the upper-right corner of the application. {name} heard the refunded fee and the fact that today's window would not reopen.

On the returned sheet, the red word was larger than the name he had meant to borrow. {name} placed the blank or refusal unfolded at the front of the file. He sent Daeun one photograph showing the stamp and one sentence: I did not file it today.

choices.text: Send Daeun the original again. Do not file until her own scope and deadline return.
choices.result_text:
From a chair beside the counter, {name} sent one image containing both the name field and the addendum. Daeun did not reply with permission to write for her. She returned one sheet bearing the permitted scope and end date in her own hand. At the bottom: I DO NOT CONSENT BEYOND THESE TERMS. HAN DAEUN.

The clerk checked her hand and date, then ruled through every field outside that scope. {name} added not one mark. Even after the filing stamp landed, a clear clip kept the consent sheet separate, dividing what Daeun had permitted from what she had not.

choices.text: Fill the field from an old identity copy that is not current consent.
choices.result_text:
{name} copied Daeun's name and number from the old sheet. The clerk asked once whether this copy recorded consent to the current scope and deadline.

"The document exists."

The answer did not meet the question, but the stamp came down. No new sentence appeared in the original message thread while the ink dried. The crease along the copy refused to flatten. {name} turned the empty chat facedown and put the filed copy deep inside his bag.

choices.text: Reduce the scale and switch to the estimate in his name alone.
choices.result_text:
The new limit fell farther from the goal. While the clerk printed the smaller figure, {name} removed every item bearing Daeun's name from the filing and wrote NOT APPLICABLE in the consenting-party field.

His name appeared only once on the filed page. He messaged Daeun: I did not use your name. No reply came at once. The thinner contract kept slipping inside the folder, with no other signature to hold it in place.

title: Two People Read His Name
description:
At 11:18 p.m., Hyunsu and Minseo sat at the same café table. The first sheet in the clear folder bore filing number 227. The deal had been reduced. NOT APPLICABLE filled the consenting-party field, and {name}'s name appeared once on the signature line.

Hyunsu looked at {name}'s face before the paper. "Hyung, remember the first night we ate ramyeon in the goshiwon hall? Whatever work you did, you still sat there with me. Don't just tell me you used only your name. Tell me how you reached this contract."

Minseo set the smaller limit beside the liability term. "You're farther from the goal, and the liability ends here. Using only your name doesn't make the choice safe by itself. It does make clear where the bill returns."

Sangchul called. RESUME SIGNING AT THE ORIGINAL LIMIT filled the screen. Neither Hyunsu nor Minseo turned the phone facedown for him.

choices.text: Hand over the filed copy. Offer no defense until both have finished reading.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu slowly compared filing number 227 with {name}'s signature. Minseo read the smaller limit and liability term, marking only the lines whose figures were correct.

{name} stayed silent through three rings of the phone. Hyunsu handed the last page to Minseo. After reading even NOT APPLICABLE, she returned the folder to the center.
"Hyung, talk about you now, not the paper," Hyunsu said. Minseo put down her pen and waited for {name}'s answer.

choices.text: Take out amendment and cancellation forms. Ask what can still be repaired.
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the blank forms beside the filed copy.
"I can't erase the choice I made. Tell me which line I can still stop or change."

Hyunsu did not pick up the pen. "If I choose your goal for you, using only your name stops meaning anything." Minseo touched only the cancellation deadline and liability term. "Procedure can still stop these two. One signature means one signer, not one affected person." They left only the lines {name} could still choose.

choices.text: Take the call and leave to resume the signing.
choices.result_text:
{name} told Sangchul, "I'm coming." Neither Hyunsu nor Minseo tried to stop him.

As he pushed back his chair, the edge of the papers lifted in the draft. Hyunsu pressed them flat with his palm. "Hyung, even on the first night, the ramyeon went cold before the goal did." Minseo closed the returns table. "The question after arrival doesn't disappear. Leaving now only makes it more exact."

After {name} closed the door, two cold cups and two sheets closed for different reasons remained on the table.

title: The Last Signature
description:
In the final month of the five years, Gangnam's lights hung beyond the window. {name} sat alone at a desk with the notebook open before him.

The notebook's first page held his starting 500,000 won beside the 3-billion-won goal that had followed him for five years. The assets screen already showed whether the current figure sat above or below it, but neither arrival nor failure could explain the time behind the result.

{name} reread only the amounts, dates, and names that were actually in the notebook. Meetings never held and answers never received stayed blank.

Money could be added and subtracted in one column. Time borrowed from people and nights never returned would not add up in the same units. The two ledgers still refused to reconcile.

The final page's blank line was only notebook paper. It was no contract or filed copy, and no stamp or filing number could appear there.

{name} read three meanings over the line. "I take responsibility." "I price the names too." "I put people first." One line; three different signatures.

Writing one would push the other two off the line. Pretending to choose all three would take responsibility for none. No one was there to sign in his place or hold the pen with him.

{name} held the black pen just above the blank line. The final decision of five years was smaller than one line, and its cost ran beyond it.

The signature itself repaid no debt and restored no distant relationship. {name} set down the pen and waited for the ink to dry. When it did, the last line held only his name.

choices.result_text:
{name} moved only names actually written in the notebook into columns for return and cost. Beside each, he recorded what he had gained, lost, and borrowed in time.

He drew every arrow toward the 3-billion-won goal. As different circumstances became units pointing the same way, voices shrank between the figures.

{name} signed his own name large on the last line. No new contract or transfer followed. When he closed the notebook, only names and arrows remained on the final page.

{name} turned off the assets screen and copied below the blank line only names that remained on the notebook's earlier pages. He added no one he had never met.

Writing a name did not mean that person was still beside him or that someone who had left had returned. {name} wrote his own name last—an order that neither pretended he had arrived alone nor turned anyone's time into decoration for his success.

No reply, meeting, or reconciliation appeared. When {name} set down the pen, only the order of names remained beside the quiet phone.

title: The Last Page Without a Stamp
description:
Seven days remained until his thirty-eighth birthday. {name} opened the final-year application beside the notebook in which he had first written the 3-billion-won goal.

The paper had no filing number and no date stamp. The consenting-party field and signature line were blank. No transfer-completion notice had arrived. Only the meeting-room coffee ring, Sangchul's red line, and the corner someone had held flat remained. {name} had seen the decision. He had carried the papers and still never returned to the counter. After the deadline, he brought the blank original home.

Every page of the notebook turned in a voice. "Minjun-ah." "Minjun." "Mr. Kim." "Hyung." Not executing the choice did not return the time those voices had spent.

Only one line remained blank on the final page. Beside the unstamped application, {name} lifted the pen.

choices.text: Write NOT FILED and today's date on the blank application.
choices.result_text:
{name} left the signature line empty. At the top of the application, in his own hand, he wrote NOT FILED and today's date.

The words did not erase the decision. They kept responsibility for not executing it inside his own time. On the notebook's last line, he wrote his name small. There was no stamp, but the person who had carried the blank paper home was clear.

choices.text: Enter the missed filing window and every remaining blank in the ledger.
choices.result_text:
{name} entered the deadline and the unfiled amount in the loss column. Beside the figures he left Sangchul's review time, Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF, and the time Daeun had spent reading the name field.

The blank application weighed less than the ledger, but it moved first whenever he closed the pages. Unable to write a new target, {name} pressed only his name into the final line.

choices.text: Write on the back the names of the people who called him back to himself.
choices.result_text:
{name} turned over the unfiled application. On the side without a stamp, he wrote the names of the people who had called him back to himself, one by one, and placed his own name last.

It was neither a declaration that he had abandoned the goal nor an excuse that he had stayed clean alone. It refused to leave as blanks the people who had spent this unexecuted night with him. {name} spoke the first name that could still answer.

title: The Same Seven Pages
description:
The copier outside the meeting room held the same seven pages twice. {name} flattened every sticky note and folded corner in Sangchul's proposal, then scanned the addendum into the same file. He did not hide the final page bearing Daeun's name field.

One send window held Sangchul's name; the other held Daeun's conversation. If the proposer and the person whose name might be used received different versions, even the order of the words could later be replaced by money's account of them. {name} compared both attachments from the first sentence to the last.

As the copier cooled, only the two blue send buttons remained. Neither window showed a read mark yet.

texts: After Sangchul was asked whether he could review his own offer, the red pen remained untouched and Father's guarantee PDF stayed open beside the seven pages. {name} had to preserve that conflict in the same file.

Beside the copier lay the version where a memo had covered Daeun's name and the calculator had stepped down to the lower terms. {name} could not send only the smaller figure and hide the name that had been covered.
Daeun had read the page bearing her name before the figures and stopped on WEEKENDS AND NIGHTS. {name} had to ensure that the original carrying her question matched Sangchul's original word for word.

choices.text: Compare both files through the final page, then send the same original in order.
choices.result_text:
After confirming page 7 of 7, {name} sent the file to Sangchul, then the identical file to Daeun two minutes later. To Sangchul he added, 'Record that the proposer and reviewer are the same person.' To Daeun: 'I did not remove the page with your name.'

No answer appeared. The same filename and two sent times remained beneath the message bubbles. {name} did not slide a blank cover sheet between them.

title: A Copy of the Red Circle
description:
On the landing outside the old office, {name} reopened the two documents Sangchul had returned. The red circle joined the guarantee PDF's liability clause to the proposal's consenting-party field; separate the pages, and only half remained on each. No time had been written on the cover. The copier downstairs was already dark.

A paper cup struck the bin behind the door, but Sangchul did not come out again. {name} needed one frame to hold both the dangerous clause and the fact that the man who had identified it was also the proposer.

The camera square caught both pages and the current capture time. The red line stayed unbroken at the center of the screen.

choices.text: Align both pages and preserve the red circle and current capture time in one frame.
choices.result_text:
{name} did not tape the guarantee PDF to the proposal. To leave no claim that he had altered the originals, he photographed the pages together, then each original separately.

He named the file PROPOSER REVIEW — RISK CLAUSE, not SANGCHUL REVIEW. When the stairwell light went out, only the red line and capture time remained bright on the screen.

title: The Clear Clip
description:
Even after the meeting ended, Daeun's handwritten sheet was not attached to the contract. In black ink it held the permitted scope, its end date, and the sentence, 'I do not consent beyond this range.' Sangchul's unverified clauses appeared below in a different hand. Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF lay in a separate stack.

Daeun picked up a clear clip. 'Don't merge them, Minjun. This isn't part of the contract. It records exactly how far I spoke.'

{name} matched the page counts on the four copies. One original remained at the center of the table, the rounded back of the clip catching the ceiling light.

choices.text: Keep the handwritten original separate from the contract, preserved by its own clip and capture time.
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote the same time at the lower-right corner of Daeun's sheet and on the contract cover, but did not staple them together. Daeun checked the photograph herself with every handwritten line visible. Sangchul initialed only beside the clauses he had not verified. No one added a signature to Jaehyuk's PDF.

After four copies disappeared into four bags, one clear clip remained on the empty table, holding the distance between the original and the contract exactly as it was.

title: Daeun Beside the Blue Pen
description:
A blue pen was tethered to the filing counter by a short metal chain. Daeun separated the pages bearing her name from those without it; the comparison's delivery time remained at the corner of its cover.

The clerk laid out four physical outcomes: a red withdrawal mark, a limited filing at the lower amount, a provisional hold with its completion time blank, and self-filing number 227 with every Daeun document removed. Looking at the blue pen, Daeun said, “Don't let the pen move past the boundary I wrote.” The number chimed again. One of those four states had to remain on paper today.

texts: At the four-person meeting, Daeun's name was struck and only the time of the smaller recalculation remained. There was no handwritten scope original.
At the four-person meeting, Daeun wrote the permitted scope and end date herself. The clerk aligned the papers only inside the boundary on that original.
At the four-person meeting, {name} chose to return to the original terms while Daeun's pen stayed beside the paper. Her name field at today's counter was still blank.
On the night the comparison was handled, Daeun took one copy into her own file. The same delivery time showed on both covers today.
On the night the comparison was handled, the copy remained sealed in {name}'s file. Daeun set apart every page she was seeing for the first time today.

choices.text: Withdraw today's application and leave only the withdrawal mark
choices.result_text:
{name} did not press Submit. He turned the application back toward the clerk, who stamped WITHDRAWN in red and wrote the time the window closed.

The queue ticket and copy receipt remained. Watching the stamp dry, Daeun said, “Not filing was your choice too. It doesn't give us back the time we spent today.”

choices.text: File only a lower limit under his own responsibility
choices.result_text: The clerk removed every field requiring another person's new consent and left only the lower limit {name} would carry. When he signed, the clerk marked the cover LIMITED FILING. The copy held that limit and the submitter's name; Daeun's hand never touched the blue pen.

choices.text: Request verification while leaving the unverified name field unresolved
choices.result_text:
{name} requested verification with the unverified name field left as it was. Instead of a final stamp, the clerk marked CURRENT CONSENT VERIFICATION HOLD and issued a provisional number.

The completion time beneath the number stayed blank, and Daeun did not take the pen. The clerk placed the page in the hold tray.

choices.text: Remove every Daeun document and file number 227 under his name alone
choices.result_text:
{name} removed every Daeun document from the submission stack and wrote NOT APPLICABLE in the consenting-party field. Only his name remained on the application signature line.

The clerk stamped number 227 and the date. Without taking a copy, Daeun said, “Not using my name isn't the same as not using my time.”

title: The Consent Sheet He Did Not Use
description:
Filing number 227 and the unused consent sheet lay side by side on the small table behind the convenience store. The filed copy said NOT APPLICABLE in the consenting-party field and bore {name}'s name once. Daeun's handwritten scope remained untouched in a separate folder.

Daeun spoke first. 'I checked that you didn't use my name. That doesn't mean you didn't use my time. The evenings I cleared to read this. The time I waited in that room with four people.'

Hyunsu looked at {name}, not the filing. 'Hyung, signing alone doesn't mean you got here alone.' Sangchul's call buzzed without ringing. Neither Daeun nor Hyunsu turned the screen over for him.

choices.text: Place both the filed copy and unused consent sheet before them, and listen to the end.
choices.result_text:
Daeun read the scope and date she had actually written, then read NOT APPLICABLE on the filed copy. Hyunsu left one finger's width between the two sheets.

{name} offered no defense until Sangchul's vibration died three times. 'You gave back the name you didn't use,' Daeun said. 'Now talk about the time you did.' Hyunsu turned the filed copy toward {name} without closing the gap.

choices.text: Take out the amendment and cancellation forms. Find only the lines he can still undo.
choices.result_text:
{name} spread the blank cancellation form without covering the filed copy. Daeun placed a finger on the cancellation deadline; Hyunsu placed his on the same-day delivery deadline. Neither chose for him.

'Stopping here costs the fee and today's window,' Daeun said. 'That's the contract's price, not the price of my forgiveness.' {name} copied both times into his notebook.

choices.text: Take Sangchul's call and return to the execution counter.
choices.result_text:
{name} told Sangchul, 'I'm coming,' and gathered the filed copy. Daeun kept her handwritten original in her own folder. Hyunsu pushed the abandoned chair back under the table. Neither blocked the door.

'Minjun.' Daeun called his name, but did not choose the next sentence for him. As the automatic door closed, filing number 227 flashed in the glass. The unused consent sheet remained at the table.

title: Daeun's Time, Minseo's Procedure
description:
Daeun and Minseo sat on opposite sides of the small table. Daeun counted the evenings she had spent on the papers; Minseo ran a fingertip from the label and number to the last state the document had reached.

“Whatever state today's paper ended in, that doesn't give me back the nights I sat here,” Daeun said. Minseo stopped at the final notation. “This still shows how far the paper got.” {name} had to decide whose words would enter the notebook first.

choices.result_text:
Daeun named the meeting night, the night she read the comparison, and the time at the counter in date order. {name} did not interrupt as he filled the first line.

Only after Daeun took her hand from the paper did Minseo write the current label and the document's last state on the second line. Their order remained.

choices.result_text:
Minseo moved her finger from the label to the number, then to the place where the last state was recorded. “Here. Nothing after this proves execution.” {name} put that location on the first line.

Daeun wrote the dates of her evenings on the second. The document state occupied the first line and the record of her time the second.

choices.text: Leave the same page open and ask each woman to write one line
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the notebook sideways between them. Daeun wrote the evenings she had spent and the hours she had waited on the left line; Minseo wrote the label and the document's last state on the right.

Neither line received a number marking it first. When both women set down their pens, two lines in different hands and measured by different standards remained on the same page.

title: Where the Money Moved
description:
The real-estate office printer swallowed the self-filed copy bearing number 227 and returned it. The consenting-party field said NOT APPLICABLE, and the limit was lower than the first proposal. Sangchul stood by the wall rather than sit on the seller's side.

The broker laid out a balance-transfer screen, a cancellation confirmation, and an assignment approval. 'Only one of these can move today. Completion sends the balance. Cancellation burns part of the deposit. Assignment moves both the settlement and the remaining liability.'

Sangchul spoke briefly. 'I brought the road. The money still moves under your hand.' None of the three signature fields yet bore {name}'s name.

choices.text: Send the balance under his own-name filing and take the execution notice.
choices.result_text:
{name} read the recipient and amount aloud, then pressed transfer. The bank tone sounded once, and the broker stamped BALANCE PERFORMED on the contract. The key remained sealed until the registry check.

The execution notice bore filing number 227, the completed transfer time, and {name}'s name alone. Sangchul checked the recipient field once more instead of offering congratulations. {name} lifted the warm sheet from the printer himself.

choices.text: Cancel the contract, accept the forfeited portion of the deposit, and receive the original cancellation confirmation.
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the transfer screen and signed the cancellation confirmation in his own name. The broker read out the refund and the portion of the deposit that would disappear. Sangchul did not offer to bargain it down.

The stamped cancellation original and refund receipt entered a clear folder. The key envelope returned to the seller's drawer. Some money remained in {name}'s account; the contract kept today's date, which would not reopen.

choices.text: Assign the purchase right and document the settlement and remaining liability.
choices.result_text:
{name} verified the new assignee and settlement figure, then signed the assignment approval. After fees and the price difference, the broker sent the balance to {name}'s account and marked one liability clause that survived the transfer.

'Getting out is still execution,' Sangchul said. Instead of answering, {name} clipped the settlement receipt to the surviving liability clause. The unopened key envelope moved to the far side of the desk.

title: Three Places for the Same Seven Pages
description:
Three copies of the same seven-page offer emerged from the conference-room printer. One went before Sangchul, one before Minseo, and one before Jiyeon. Their sentences matched from first page to last; their sent times differed by seconds.

Sangchul occupied the seats of proposer and counterparty. Minseo held a gray pencil instead of a red pen. “I'll mark what I verified separately from what Mr. Sangchul promised.” Jiyeon read that her name could enter a joint-liability field but did not take a pen.

“Oppa, we're not at the point of using my name yet, right?”

{name} showed her the blank signature line. The choice now was not consent, but what all three would see first in the same original.

choices.text: Mark first the difference between the total and the liability cap.
choices.result_text:
{name} marked the total and the joint-liability cap in different colors. Sangchul began to discuss returns, then stopped. Minseo wrote in the margin the conditions under which the two figures diverged.

Jiyeon studied the line that ended beside her name longer than the largest number. The size of the money came forward; custody of the copies and the review deadline remained on later pages.

choices.text: Open first the field where Jiyeon's name could appear and the conditions on its use.
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the joint-liability field beside the appendix governing name use. Jiyeon confirmed that her name had not been printed, then left the page corner unfolded.

“A blank isn't permission.” Minseo copied Jiyeon's sentence into the first line of her review note. The name came forward, and the returns table moved one page back.

choices.text: Have Minseo read aloud the clauses she could not verify first.
choices.result_text:
Minseo drew three small boxes in gray pencil: the termination time, the copy-retention period, and the condition that expanded joint liability.

“If these have no answer today, I can't mark the review complete.” Sangchul checked the clock once. Jiyeon wrote her own question beside each box. Review time grew, and the time left to preserve the day's terms shrank by the same amount.

title: Five People in the Room
description:
Five chairs filled the conference room. Sangchul had the seven-page offer; Minseo, an identical copy with gray pencil marks; Jiyeon, a copy open to the joint-liability field. Jaehyuk held his guarantee PDF upright on his lap. Only a calculator sat before {name}.

“I brought the terms, but that isn't the same as Ms. Minseo's review,” Sangchul said. Minseo began where his red marks and her gray boxes did not overlap. Jaehyuk said, “My name is on the guarantee side too.” Jiyeon covered her blank field with one palm.

The five sets of papers pointed in different directions beneath the wall clock. Whichever document moved to the center first would push another question behind it.

choices.text: Align the offer, review copy, and guarantee PDF. Have each person read their own field.
choices.result_text:
{name} aligned the three documents without removing their staples. Sangchul read the offer amount, Minseo the three unverified clauses, and Jaehyuk his guarantee cap.

Jiyeon spoke last, stating that the joint-liability field was blank. Each of the four voices remained once in the room, but the reading took the most time. The minute hand moved one mark closer to the transfer lock.

choices.text: Have Minseo ask first where Sangchul's proposal conflicts with his review.
choices.result_text:
Minseo set her copy beside, not over, Sangchul's returns table. “These are the parts you called safe that I haven't verified.”

Sangchul lowered the red pen instead of arguing. Jaehyuk could not close his guarantee PDF. Jiyeon copied the three gray boxes onto her own sheet. The conflict was exposed, but Jaehyuk's reason for returning and Jiyeon's scope moved behind it.

choices.text: Give Jiyeon a blank page before anyone reads the numbers.
choices.result_text:
{name} turned over the calculator and put a blank page before Jiyeon. She wrote three questions: What cap can I carry? Does anything take effect before review ends? Which copies must remain?

Sangchul rolled his pen without starting the calculation. Jaehyuk covered his PDF's empty signature line. Minseo left an unverified gray box at the end of each question. No answer was fixed, and only the time for negotiating numbers grew shorter.

title: The Three Lines Jiyeon Narrowed
description:
9:41 p.m. Minseo's three gray boxes were still open. Sangchul's calculator showed the lower limit if Jiyeon's name came out. Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF lay closed at the edge of the table.

At the bottom of the blank page Jiyeon wrote: I DO NOT CONSENT BEYOND THIS SCOPE. She looked at {name}. “Before we discuss why you want my name, I'm deciding what I can be responsible for.”

A lower liability cap meant less available money. Requiring completed independent review consumed tonight's time. A wider destruction rule removed backup copies that might be useful later. Each route left the same limited consent and refusal beyond it in Jiyeon's hand, but took a different thing now.

choices.text: Fix Jiyeon's liability cap as a number and strike every amount above it.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon wrote one joint-liability cap and its end date on the same line, then struck the amounts above it. {name} copied into his notebook the lower limit Sangchul recalculated.

The amount Sangchul could offer fell, while Jaehyuk's guarantee cap did not change. Minseo checked Jiyeon's figure against the end of the clause and left one gray verification mark. Jiyeon kept the pen before her instead of returning it.

choices.text: Make consent valid only after Minseo completes independent review.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon wrote ONLY AFTER MINSEO'S REVIEW IS COMPLETE above the name field. Minseo read the three open clauses and the time each required.

The review could not finish before tonight's lock. Sangchul said the day's terms might disappear, but Jiyeon did not erase the sentence. {name} watched the empty completion time rather than the shrinking clock. The gray boxes remained.

choices.text: Keep Jiyeon's original and Minseo's review copy, and place Sangchul's identical copy within the destruction scope.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon allowed only her own copy and one bearing Minseo's review marks to remain. Sangchul's one identical copy went onto a numbered destruction list.

{name} lost one backup document he might have reopened later. Sangchul checked the count, and Minseo wrote down the first and last sentences for comparison before destruction. Jiyeon pressed the sentence refusing anything beyond scope once more.

title: Gray Marks and Jiyeon's Hand
description:
After the meeting, three kinds of marks remained on the table: Jiyeon's limited consent and refusal beyond it, Minseo's gray boxes separating verified from unverified lines, and a first-and-last-page comparison showing the three copies shared one original.

{name} aligned only the upper corners of Jiyeon's original, Minseo's review sheet, and the matching-copy comparison. Sangchul's calculations and Jaehyuk's guarantee PDF remained open at opposite ends of the table, a handspan from the clear clip.

One clear clip held only Jiyeon's original, Minseo's review sheet, and that comparison. The wall clock had crossed into the next minute. The final stroke of the refusal remained visible beneath the clip.

choices.result_text:
{name} aligned the upper corners and attached the clear clip. Jiyeon's limited consent went first, Minseo's gray-marked review second, and the same-original confirmation with its preservation time last.

The clip held only the three pages that remained when the meeting ended. Sangchul's calculations and Jaehyuk's PDF returned to their own files. Jiyeon pressed the clip once, then turned the packet until her original faced her.

title: Jiyeon's Name at the Filing Counter
description:
The blue pen at the filing counter was tethered by a short metal chain. Jiyeon stood opposite the clerk, not beside {name}, moving between her limited-consent original and Minseo's gray review sheet.

“Oppa, my cap and end date stop here.” Jiyeon pressed a nail beneath her refusal beyond scope. The clerk checked the liability cap, Minseo's verified and unverified marks, and copy-retention terms against the contract. A withdrawal stamp sat on one side, a filing stamp on the other, and an electronic form capable of copying her name beyond the limit glowed on the screen.

The number sounded again. Today could leave one thing: withdrawal, limited filing, use beyond scope, or a smaller filing in his name alone.

choices.text: Acknowledge the clauses beyond Jiyeon's scope and withdraw today's filing.
choices.result_text:
{name} did not lift the blue pen. The clerk stamped WITHDRAWN at the upper right and read the nonrefundable fee and the counter time that would not reopen today.

Jiyeon did not thank him. She placed her original and Minseo's review sheet in a clear folder. “Not filing was your choice, Oppa. My name didn't make it clean.” They held opposite ends of the paper until the red ink dried.

choices.text: File only within Jiyeon's written limit and strike every remaining field.
choices.result_text:
The clerk compared Jiyeon's hand, date, and Minseo's verified and unverified marks, then ruled through every line beyond scope. After hearing the reduced limit, {name} filled his own signature field. Jiyeon signed the limited-consenting-party field once, matching her original.

The filing stamp and number did not bind her original to the contract. One filed copy slid toward Jiyeon. She left it on the counter and began by reading where her name ended.

choices.text: Attach Jiyeon's original and electronically file her name in the fields beyond its limit.
choices.result_text:
{name} attached the limited-consent original, then entered Jiyeon's name in fields beyond it. “Did she consent to this line today?” the clerk asked. Jiyeon raised her head first.

“No. That's the line I struck.” Instead of the final stamp, the clerk marked SCOPE CHECK PENDING and issued a temporary number. Jiyeon removed her original. Her entered name and the hold notice remained together on the screen.

choices.text: Remove Jiyeon's materials and switch to the smaller estimate in his name alone.
choices.result_text:
The new limit stood farther from the goal. {name} removed Jiyeon's original and the personal portions of the review sheet, wrote NOT APPLICABLE in the consenting-party field, and left only his own name in the signature line.

While the clerk stamped the smaller filing, Jiyeon read the reduced figure to the end. “Not using my name isn't the same as not using my time.” Each took one copy of the thinner packet.

title: The Filed Copy Placed in Jiyeon's Hands
description:
Two copies filed within Jiyeon's limit still held the counter's warmth. Both bore the same filing number and time, the liability cap and end date in Jiyeon's hand, and the lines struck beyond scope.

The clerk placed one copy toward {name} and one toward Jiyeon. Before taking hers, Jiyeon compared the signature positions on the original and the filed copy. “Only the lines I agreed to are in here, right?”

{name} pointed to the matching lines and pushed Jiyeon's copy toward her. The clerk tapped the small receipt-time box. Jiyeon had not yet reached for the paper. As the counter clock advanced, the blue pen's metal chain stretched taut between the two warm copies.

choices.text: Hand one limited filing copy directly to Jiyeon and record the delivery time.
choices.result_text:
{name} placed Jiyeon's copy in a clear envelope and handed it over with both hands. He wrote only the filing number and delivery time on the front. Jiyeon did not say thank you or that it was all right. She turned the envelope until the lines beyond scope faced her.

The counter clock moved one minute. One copy remained in {name}'s hand and its twin in Jiyeon's. The blue pen's metal chain stretched between the envelopes.

title: Two Thresholds in the Same Filed Copy
description:
On the late-night cafe table, Jiyeon's limited filing copy lay beside {name}'s twin. The liability cap, end date, lines struck beyond scope, and filing number repeated across both pages.

Jiyeon spoke first about the doors the paper could open. “This changes which rooms we can enter. That's why my boundary has to be exact.” Hyunsu looked at the two of them rather than the filing number. “Hyung, even if more doors open, whose name opened them doesn't disappear.”

Sangchul's call vibrated on the screen: ARE YOU COMING BACK TO THE EXECUTION COUNTER TODAY? Jiyeon and Hyunsu held the same paper for different reasons. Neither answered for him.

choices.text: Offer no defense while both read the same filed copy to the end.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon read where her name began and ended. Hyunsu read {name}'s signature and filing time, leaving one finger's width between the two copies.

{name} said nothing until Sangchul's vibration died three times. “Access doesn't grant you the right to cross my line,” Jiyeon said. Hyunsu turned the filed copy toward {name} without closing the gap.

choices.text: Take out amendment and cancellation forms. Ask only what can still be undone.
choices.result_text:
{name} spread the blank amendment and cancellation forms without covering the filed copy. Jiyeon pointed to the cancellation time; Hyunsu pointed to the number on the delivered copy.

“Stopping costs today's terms and the fee,” Jiyeon said. “That cost isn't the same as my answer.” Hyunsu chose nothing for him and told him to write first what he could afford to lose. The two blank forms remained on either side of the filed copy.

choices.text: Take Sangchul's call and return to the execution counter.
choices.result_text:
{name} told Sangchul, “I'm coming,” and gathered his own filed copy. Jiyeon kept hers in the clear envelope. Hyunsu pushed the abandoned chair under the table.

“Oppa.” Jiyeon called, but did not choose the next sentence for him. The filing number flashed in the glass as the automatic door closed. Jiyeon's copy and Hyunsu's unfinished water remained on the table.

title: Money Moving Behind the Limit
description:
The real-estate office printer returned the filing bearing Jiyeon's limited consent. Lines outside the liability cap and end date were struck. Sangchul stood by the wall rather than take the seller's chair.

The broker aligned a balance-transfer screen, cancellation confirmation, and assignment approval. “Only one can move today. Completion sends the balance. Cancellation loses part of the deposit. Assignment transfers both settlement and surviving liability.”

Jiyeon already held her copy. The paper here was the twin {name} had carried back. “The consent line is fixed,” Sangchul said. “Which document moves the money is now under your hand.”

choices.text: Send the balance under the limited-consent filing and receive the original execution confirmation.
choices.result_text:
{name} read the recipient, balance, and Jiyeon's liability cap, then pressed transfer. The bank tone sounded once, and the broker stamped BALANCE PERFORMED on the contract.

The original confirmation printed the filing number, completed-transfer time, and end of the limited consent together. The key stayed sealed pending registry verification. Sangchul checked the recipient instead of congratulating him. {name} lifted one warm original himself.

choices.text: Cancel the contract and receive the cancellation original with the portion of the deposit lost.
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the transfer screen and signed the cancellation confirmation. The broker read the refund and the portion of the deposit that disappeared separately. Jiyeon's consent did not expand, but today's terms closed.

The stamped cancellation original and refund receipt entered one envelope. The key returned to the seller's drawer. Sangchul offered no way to bargain down the loss.

choices.text: Assign the purchase right and document the settlement and surviving liability.
choices.result_text:
{name} verified the assignee and settlement, then signed the assignment approval. The broker sent the settlement after fees and the price difference, and marked the one liability line that survived assignment.

“Getting out is still execution,” Sangchul said. {name} clipped the settlement receipt to the surviving clause. The unopened key envelope moved to the far side of the desk.

title: The Time the Execution Original Crossed Hands
description:
Jiyeon waited at the end of the real-estate office corridor. {name} held one original execution confirmation and one matching copy. Both showed the filing number, completed-transfer time, and the line where Jiyeon's limited consent ended. The key remained in the broker's desk pending registry verification.

Before taking a copy, Jiyeon asked, “Oppa, does the same page show the money you sent and the limit I carry?”

{name} opened the original and showed that the lines did not overlap. Two empty clear envelopes and a pen for the receipt time lay on the corridor bench. Jiyeon left the edge of the original untouched and read again from the line where her name stopped.

choices.text: Hand one original execution confirmation to Jiyeon and record the received time.
choices.result_text:
{name} put Jiyeon's original in a clear envelope. On the front he wrote only the filing number and received time, adding neither congratulations nor safety.

Jiyeon took it and read the end of her limited consent, then the completed-transfer time. She did not say it was all right. The matching copy remained with {name}. On the corridor floor, the shadows of the two envelopes lengthened without touching.

title: The Copy Placed Before the Key
description:
On the day the registry check was stamped, the broker placed the key envelope and execution copy on one tray. Jiyeon sat across from {name}, beginning again at the line where her limited consent ended. Metal inside the envelope made a small sound against the tray.

When {name} reached for the key first, Jiyeon pressed the corner of the execution copy. “Oppa, looking at this door together isn't the same as lending you my name forever.”

Jiyeon turned her body toward neither the key nor the door. She needed room to name the cost of having stayed through this scene. {name} lowered the key and turned the execution copy toward her.

choices.text: Put down the key and let Jiyeon finish naming the cost of remaining.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon touched the liability cap and end date once each. “Even while I'm sitting here, this line remains mine. On the next document, don't make my place before waiting for my answer.”

{name} copied the sentence into the margin without defending himself. Jiyeon did not sign. The broker left the tray in place. One blue pen lay across the space between the key envelope and the limited execution copy.

title: The Final Page with Two Names
description:
Seven days remained until his thirty-eighth birthday. Beside the notebook where he had first written KRW 3 billion, {name} opened Jiyeon's limited-consent filing and the matching execution copy. One held Jiyeon's name and the end of her liability; the other held the actual transfer time and {name}'s signature.

Minseo's gray marks, Sangchul's red line, and the name Hyunsu had questioned remained. The key envelope stayed closed at the edge of the desk.

Only one line remained blank. Execution in his own name could not erase the other person's consent that opened the door. The line could own responsibility, price those names again, or place people's time first.

choices.text: Write his name on the last line and take responsibility beyond Jiyeon's limit.
choices.result_text:
{name} aligned his signature on the execution confirmation with the blank notebook line. He did not erase Jiyeon's name. Beneath it he wrote, RESPONSIBILITY BEYOND THIS LINE BELONGS TO {name}.

The black name, limited boundary, and transfer time remained in one frame. He did not open the key. When he set down the pen, one line of paper separated Jiyeon's hand from his.

choices.text: Put Jiyeon's name and Minseo's time into the cost column and calculate once more.
choices.result_text:
{name} moved Jiyeon's limited consent, Minseo's review time, and Sangchul's route into columns of return and cost. Beside the executed money, people's names moved closer to numbers again.

He wrote his own name large on the final line. The pen pressed through the execution confirmation and repeated the stroke on the next sheet. Metal in the key envelope sounded once at the desk's edge.

choices.text: Write first the names of those who called him by name, and place his own last.
choices.result_text:
{name} turned off the asset screen and flipped the filed copy. On the blank side he wrote Jiyeon, Minseo, Hyunsu, Sangchul, Jaehyuk, and Father, one name at a time. His own came last.

The limited consent and execution responsibility did not disappear. But people's time stood before the execution confirmation. {name} opened the first contact that could still answer and read one name aloud from the page.

title: The Empty Guarantee Chair
description:
The conference room had four chairs, but only three were occupied. Sangchul had the seven-page offer he brought and a red pen. Daeun had a copy open to the name field and her explicit refusal original. {name} had a calculator. Jaehyuk's chair was empty. The blocked chat remained on its last bubble, and the guarantee attachment field was blank.

“If I'm both proposer and reviewer, you read my word twice,” Sangchul said. “Leave what I couldn't verify separate.” Daeun set her refusal beside, not over, her name field. “{name}, my absence doesn't erase my answer.”

The empty guarantee field, Sangchul's conflict, and Daeun's refusal shared the desk. Moving one to the center exposed a different present loss.

choices.text: Have Sangchul separate his proposal marks from his review marks in different colors.
choices.result_text:
Sangchul marked offered terms in red and unverified clauses in gray. The two colors diverged more often than they overlapped.

{name} gained no verdict of safety and lost time before the day's lock. Daeun pulled the gray-marked copy toward herself. “At least the lines nobody knows are marked as unknown.”

choices.text: Open the empty guarantee field and ask first how the amount changes without Jaehyuk.
choices.result_text:
{name} left the guarantee appendix empty and asked Sangchul for the revised limit. Sangchul placed the old figure and the lower figure on opposite sides of the calculator.

No new name appeared to replace Jaehyuk. The gap stayed on the screen. Daeun checked first that her refusal had actually removed her name. The unfilled field looked wider.

choices.text: Before the numbers, have Daeun make the copy with her name removed herself.
choices.result_text:
Daeun ruled through her name field and wrote I DO NOT CONSENT. {name} copied the page before hearing how far the terms would fall.

Sangchul began recalculating, and time to preserve the day's terms shrank. Daeun compared the same place on both copies. Between Jaehyuk's empty chair and the empty guarantee field, the place where her name had been remained black.

title: Closing Three Empty Fields
description:
9:46 p.m. Daeun's I DO NOT CONSENT original remained beside her name field. Jaehyuk's guarantee field remained empty. On Sangchul's copy, proposal marks and unverified marks had split into two colors.

Daeun looked at {name}. “Leaving only your name doesn't erase my refusal. Leave the lost money and the lines Mr. Sangchul couldn't verify too.” Sangchul took his hand from the calculator. “I brought this road. I can't certify it as safe.”

Removing the name lowered the limit. Removing conflicted clauses required more time. Closing the empty guarantee appendix erased backup financing. Every route removed Daeun's name and narrowed the document to his alone, but lost something different now.

choices.text: Delete Daeun's name and accept the lower limit in his name alone.
choices.result_text:
{name} struck both Daeun's name field and the joint-liability line, then wrote that the consenting-party field did not apply to this filing. Sangchul read the new limit, and he wrote its difference from the old terms on the same page.

Daeun did not thank him. “That number belongs to you now, {name}.” The empty guarantee field was marked as carrying no guarantee. The lower limit, his name, and Daeun's refusal remained on separate lines of one page.

choices.text: Remove the clauses Sangchul could not verify independently and make a new self-name copy.
choices.result_text:
{name} separated the gray-marked clauses from the contract. Sangchul said the recalculation might cross tonight's lock.

The day's chance weakened, but proposal and review did not merge into one claim. Daeun's name appeared nowhere on the new copy, and the empty guarantee field closed. The fresh paper from the printer was thinner and carried none of the unverified lines.

choices.text: Close the guarantee appendix and request a new estimate using no name but his own.
choices.result_text:
{name} removed the empty guarantee appendix and asked Sangchul to rewrite what his name alone could support. Sangchul entered a lower amount and a later deadline.

No one replaced Jaehyuk's absence. Daeun took back her refusal original. {name} lost the backup document and the day's speed. NOT APPLICABLE remained in the consenting-party field of the new estimate.

title: A Refusal Kept in Three Copies
description:
After the meeting, three separate pages lay on the copier. Daeun's original held her explicit refusal and date. The self-name reduction showed the place her name had left and stated that the empty guarantee field carried no guarantee. Sangchul's review sheet kept the clauses he had not verified in gray.

The blocked chat had stopped at its last bubble, and the guarantee attachment field remained blank. {name} kept Daeun's refusal, removal of her name, and Sangchul's unknowns on separate pages. Only the unsigned corners of the three sheets overlapped in the copier glass. As it cooled, the mouths of three clear envelopes faced different directions.

choices.text: Preserve the refusal original, self-name reduction, and unverified-clause sheet in separate envelopes.
choices.result_text:
{name} placed Daeun's refusal before her, the self-name reduction before himself, and Sangchul's unverified-clause sheet at the center. He wrote only the document title and preservation time on each envelope.

None of the three envelopes bore a new signature or guarantee number. Daeun took her envelope. Sangchul did not sign the center one. Only the copy stating that no guarantee was used remained in {name}'s hands, reflecting the copier light.

title: Only Two People at the Filing Counter
description:
Only {name} and the clerk stood at the filing counter. The blue pen was tethered by a short chain. Of the three clear envelopes, only a copy of Daeun's refusal original lay on the comparison surface. The smaller self-name filing said the consenting-party field did not apply and the guarantee field carried no guarantee.

The clerk moved between the refusal date and the erased name field. The screen showed both a field where Daeun's erased name could be reentered and a button for holding the packet without filing.

Neither Daeun nor Sangchul was present. What could remain now was one of four physical states: withdrawal, self-name filing, reentry of the name from the refusal copy, or an unfiled hold.

choices.text: After checking Daeun's refusal, withdraw today's filing.
choices.result_text:
{name} lowered the blue pen. The clerk stamped WITHDRAWN and read the nonrefundable fee and the counter's closing time.

Daeun's name was never entered, and the smaller self-name form was not filed. While the red stamp dried, {name} kept the refusal copy and empty consenting-party field in separate envelopes. The counter number sounded once more.

choices.text: Remove every Daeun document and file only the smaller form in his own name.
choices.result_text:
The clerk retained Daeun's refusal only as a comparison record and removed it from the filing stack. {name} reread that the consenting-party field did not apply and the guarantee field carried no guarantee, then signed in his own name.

Filing number 227 and the date stamp landed on the smaller form. The limit was lower; no other signature appeared. The clerk offered two copies. {name} put one in his own envelope and the second in a clear envelope with no address.

choices.text: Copy the name from the refusal sheet into the erased name field again.
choices.result_text:
{name} copied the name from the refusal sheet into the erased name field again. “Do you have a current consent original?” the clerk asked. Only the refusal copy lay on the comparison surface.

Instead of a final stamp, the clerk marked CURRENT CONSENT CHECK PENDING. A temporary number appeared, but the completion time stayed blank. The clerk preserved the refusal copy and entry screen together in the hold record. The question remained aimed at an empty chair.

choices.text: Sign nothing and take the smaller form away in an unfiled state.
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the screen without pressing submit. The clerk wrote only the deadline on the unstamped form and returned it.

It was neither withdrawal nor filing. Daeun's name had not been used, but {name}'s had not entered the signature field either. He placed both copies in an envelope and stepped away. The blue pen's chain swayed over the empty counter.

title: The Second Envelope Without an Address
description:
Two copies of the smaller self-name filing carried the same number 227 and date stamp. The consenting-party field said it did not apply, the guarantee field stated that no guarantee was used, and {name}'s name appeared once in the signature line.

One entered his own clear envelope. He placed the second in a separate envelope that could have gone to Daeun, but left the recipient line blank. His last chat with Daeun remained open on the phone, its input field empty.

Only the filing time remained between the addressless envelope and the empty input field. The choice in his hands was to preserve the unsent copy and its time as they were.

choices.text: Do not send the second envelope. Mark only UNDELIVERED, the time, and filing number.
choices.result_text:
{name} wrote UNDELIVERED and the current time at the upper right instead of filling the recipient line. He left the phone's input empty and turned the screen face down.

The face-down screen faintly reflected the ceiling. One copy stayed in his envelope; its twin remained in a desk drawer. When the drawer closed, a corner of the clear plastic caught briefly, then folded inside.

title: Notice of Money That Did Not Move
description:
After the execution deadline, Sangchul's seven-page original remained open on the desk. The balance-transfer screen showed no completion time. No cancellation stamp or assignment approval existed. Only self-name filing number 227 remained in its clear envelope.

The last call screen from Sangchul still read RESUME SIGNING AT THE ORIGINAL LIMIT. No later question or demand had arrived. {name} had to speak first.

The unsigned final page and empty transfer time remained side by side with the screen. What he could send now was that no money moved, the original remained with him, and the time of that notice.

choices.text: Tell Sangchul first that there was no transfer or execution, and preserve the open original's current time.
choices.result_text:
{name} sent: ‘I did not transfer the balance today, and the contract was not executed. I still hold the original.’ The attached photo showed only the unsigned final page and the clock.

A sent time appeared beneath the bubble, followed only by empty screen. {name} did not reopen the transfer screen. He put the original in a clear envelope, leaving the final digits of filing number 227 visible.

title: Notice That No Executable Contract Exists
description:
On the day of the non-transfer notice, {name} placed the counter paper beside Daeun and Minseo's memo on one screen. A label and number remained, but there was no purchase price, payment term, or completed original. These pages gave him nothing he could hand to a bank as a transfer instruction.

The message field to Sangchul was empty. {name} could state first where the papers had stopped. The closing time, the evenings both women had spent, and the comparison copy delivered or kept would remain after the notice was sent.

After the sent time appeared, the account still showed no new transfer, and no ownership or debt document had been created. {name} returned the comparison and filing papers to their established custody.

title: Documents to Return Instead of a Key
description:
There was no key envelope on the cafe table before Hyunsu. Instead lay self-name filing number 227, the sent record telling Sangchul there had been no transfer or execution, and the seven-page original that still had to be returned. Its final signature field and completed-transfer time were blank.

Hyunsu flattened a corner before reading the figures. “Hyung, this time you didn't hold the door with someone else's name.” He placed the filing beside the sent record. “But the time people spent reading all this didn't disappear.”

{name} opened a return-preparation envelope beside the empty place where a key might have been. As Hyunsu read the three records again as people's time, the recipient line stayed blank and the corners of all seven original pages remained outside the envelope.

choices.text: Open the filed copy, no-execution record, and original to return. Hear Hyunsu to the end.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu read the filing number, sent time, and blank signature line. “Filing in your name and not sending the money were both things you did, Hyung. You didn't use a person as collateral, but that doesn't erase how long people waited.”

{name} offered no defense. He placed the original in a separate envelope marked RETURN PREPARED and left the recipient line blank. A cold glass of water and the unsealed envelope remained where a key might have been.

title: A Filing Stamp and an Empty Transfer Time
description:
Seven days remained until his thirty-eighth birthday. Beside the notebook where he had first written KRW 3 billion, {name} opened his self-name filing and the contract original prepared for return. The filing bore number 227, a date stamp, and his name. The execution signature and balance-transfer time were blank. There was no key.

The record of checking Daeun's refusal, Sangchul's unverified clauses, and the no-execution notice Hyunsu read remained between earlier pages. Filing had not moved the money. Not executing had not returned people's time.

Only the notebook's last line was blank. At the pen tip, the question split: under what name could he carry both the stamped choice and the contract that had not moved?

choices.text: Write that both the filing and non-execution were his choices, then sign his name.
choices.result_text:
{name} copied the filing number and sent time of the no-execution notice onto one line. Beneath them he wrote, BOTH THE FILING AND THE MONEY NOT SENT WERE CHOICES MADE BY {name}, then placed his name.

The stamp remained, but no completed-transfer mark appeared. The black name and blank execution field shared one frame. When he set down the pen, the final page of the return-prepared original lifted and settled.

choices.text: Put the filed name and missed execution time into the cost column and calculate.
choices.result_text:
{name} entered Sangchul's review time, Daeun's refusal, and the night before Hyunsu into the cost column. The filing number went under assets; the unmoved money and closed deadline went under loss.

The ledger grew more exact while people's voices shrank between figures. His name pressed long into the final line. Only the calculator's cold light remained beside the empty transfer time.

choices.text: Write first on the back of the filing the names of those who called him by name.
choices.result_text:
{name} flipped the filed copy and wrote Daeun, Hyunsu, Minseo, Sangchul, Jaehyuk, and Father in order. His own name came last.

The contract did not become executed, and the filing did not disappear. But people's time stood before the stamp and empty transfer time. {name} opened the first contact that could still answer and read one name aloud from the page.
